title: Operator & internal AI availability
summary: Operator is documented as an in-workspace assistant for inspecting and editing configuration, not as a fifth guest-facing product or a standalone SKU. Internal agents are a separate V3 agent type; public sources do not support selling either as autonomous operations software.
markdown:
Operator shows up in Conduit’s docs and as a line on the Messaging package, not as a peer of [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), or [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). Treat it as an internal configuration assistant unless a later source says otherwise. Internal agents are a V3 agent class, not a packaged “internal AI” offering on the marketing site.

## What is established

The public product nav lists Agents, Inbox, Portals, Workflows, and a fifth item labeled **Operations · Coming soon** (housekeeping, maintenance, inspections). The site footer names Conduit Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows. Operator is not in that product set. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Docs describe Operator as **Conduit’s workspace assistant** used to inspect, edit, and reason about agent configuration, listed under Test And Deploy next to sandbox testing. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/) The agents overview puts Operator on the Build surfaces (with Knowledge, Skills, Tools, and Sandbox) and says it helps teams inspect and update workspace configuration. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work) The docs index repeats the same job: inspect, edit, and reason about the workspace. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/llms.txt)

V3 setup includes **external, internal, and voice** agents. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/) That is an agent type, not a SKU. The index also lists an Internal Agent Use Cases gallery; that page was not in the supplied passages, so no gallery examples are claimed. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/llms.txt)

The REST API uses “operator replies” for **human** sends. `is_sent_by_autopilot` is true only when Conduit’s AI agent generated and sent the message, and false for operator replies, workflow sends, and messages ingested from a connected channel. Do not read that flag as the Operator assistant. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

## Role in the product system

| Name in sources | What it is on the page | Relation to guests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operator / AI operator | Workspace assistant; Build surface | Not described as guest-facing |
| Internal agents | V3 agent type with customer and voice | Staff-oriented by name only |
| Operations (nav) | Coming soon: housekeeping, maintenance, inspections | Unreleased on marketing pages |
| Guest agents | Answer messages and calls; act in connected tools | Guest-facing |

MCP treats Operator skills as their own object (`operatorSettings.skills`), separate from regular agent skills. `operator_*` tools manage the knowledge cards the Operator assistant uses, match the Operator settings screen, need workspace scope and Manage Agents, and are **MCP-only** (no matching REST route). [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

Changelog 3.12 (11 Sep 2026) mentions the AI operator in workflow-builder fixes and timezone display, which fits an in-app assistant rather than a guest channel. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/changelog)

Do not merge Operator with coming-soon Operations, with guest [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), or with [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows).

## Use cases and users

Only uses named in these passages, without adding autonomy:

- Inspect, edit, and reason about agent configuration while testing and deploying V3 agents. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)
- Inspect and update workspace configuration as a Build surface. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)
- Manage Operator skills (the assistant’s knowledge cards) over MCP, distinct from agent skills. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)
- Changelog 3.12: update tasks, including custom fields, from the AI operator; Operator timestamps in the workspace timezone. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/changelog)
- Docs index: devices can be managed with agents, workflows, Operator, or MCP. The Devices page itself is not in this evidence set, so Operator device actions are not listed. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/llms.txt)

Likely users are workspace admins and people who configure agents. Internal agents can be created in V3; their jobs are unknown here.

## Availability and dependencies

The Messaging package lists **Operator, workflows, escalation** among included items. Starting rate shown is $18 / unit / mo, with 40 credits / unit / mo; pricing scales beyond 50 listings. That is a **bundle line**, not a standalone Operator price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

REST API and MCP are described as available on the v3 plan, enabled via support@conduit.ai. Operator-skill tools exist only on MCP. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

Not established: whether every workspace gets Operator by default, credit cost for Operator chats, UI role gates beyond Manage Agents for MCP skill writes, or how internal agents are licensed. See [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) and [Developer platform & custom workflows](#knowledge/product-developers).

## What sales can say

Accurate: Operator is Conduit’s in-workspace assistant for inspecting and editing configuration; Messaging copy includes Operator with workflows and escalation; it is not one of the four named guest products and is not the coming-soon Operations module.

Do not claim Operator is a standalone product, runs guest operations end to end, acts without a person, replaces staff, or has its own published price. Do not reuse Level 4 “autonomous operator” language from the automation-levels essay as a current feature; that page labels Level 4 as the future. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/the-5-levels-of-ai-automation)

Guest automation belongs on [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) and [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). Confirm entitlements on a live quote.

## Questions to resolve

The Operator docs page and Internal Agent Use Cases gallery were not in the supplied passages, so UI, limits, and staff-agent examples are open. It is also unclear whether Messaging “Operator,” the V3 assistant, and changelog “AI operator” are one surface; which tasks Operator can update; which device actions it can run; and how Operator and internal agents are gated versus MCP `operator_*` tools.
open_questions: What does the Operator settings/UI page actually allow (action catalog, limits, who can open it) beyond inspect/edit/reason copy?
Are Messaging-package “Operator,” the V3 workspace assistant, and changelog “AI operator” the same surface?
What internal-agent jobs exist on the Internal Agent Use Cases gallery page?
Which task types, fields, and permissions apply to “update tasks… from the AI operator” in changelog 3.12?
Which device actions can Operator perform versus agents, workflows, and MCP?
How are Operator, internal agents, and MCP operator_* tools gated (plan, credits, roles) in production workspaces?
